headline: Nigeria's election commission said it will use artificial intelligence to help check results and detect cyberattacks before the 2027 elections.
score_reason: Facts match the headline, but details and independent checks are missing and the claims rest on the commission's own statement.
importance_line: It affects Nigerian voters and observers because AI would be used in checking election results, yet the commission has not said exactly how it works, who audits it or which companies supply it.
summary: Sahara Reporters reports that Joash Amupitan, chairman of Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), said on 6 Oct 2026 that the commission has set up an AI division and already uses automated AI auditing tools to verify results, under mandatory human oversight and a five-pillar governance framework whose policy is still being finalised. He added that AI tools made with unnamed international partners will watch database traffic for cyber intrusions, while some Nigerians online asked what the AI will actually do and who will audit it.
notes: Single outlet reporting the chairman's own claims; social-media reactions are individual posts.
